title: Trace intelligence from source to consumer and back
description: Switch scenarios to see where normalization, enrichment, analyst judgment, sharing policy, action policy, and consumer feedback change the result. Select any component to inspect its responsibility.

nodes.label: Intelligence source
nodes.detail: Provides reports, observations, feeds, or partner submissions under a documented provenance and sharing agreement.

nodes.label: Ingestion connector
nodes.detail: Authenticates to the source, checkpoints progress, preserves source identity, and quarantines malformed or unexpectedly large payloads.

nodes.label: Normalize + deduplicate
nodes.detail: Maps source fields into stable objects and relationships, resolves duplicates, and keeps conflicting claims instead of silently overwriting them.

nodes.label: Knowledge store
nodes.detail: Keeps observables, indicators, actors, campaigns, sightings, relationships, confidence, validity, provenance, and markings as queryable state.

nodes.label: Enrichment services
nodes.detail: Adds bounded context such as passive DNS, sandbox results, vulnerability links, or internal sightings while recording provider and observation time.

nodes.label: Analyst review
nodes.detail: Tests the source claim against context, resolves conflicts, documents uncertainty, and decides which downstream uses are justified.

nodes.label: Sharing + action gate
nodes.detail: Enforces marking, audience, freshness, confidence, false-positive, approval, expiry, and destination-specific action rules.

nodes.label: Security consumer
nodes.detail: Uses approved intelligence in a SIEM, EDR, firewall, case system, hunt workflow, report, or partner collection under an explicit contract.

nodes.label: Sightings + outcomes
nodes.detail: Returns matches, false positives, analyst dispositions, disablement events, and control outcomes so confidence and policy can be revised.

scenarios.label: Curated alert
scenarios.summary: A partner report is normalized, enriched, reviewed, released as a reviewable alert, and updated when the consumer returns a disposition.
scenarios.result: The consumer receives evidence with provenance, context, a bounded action, and an expiry path. Feedback can strengthen, weaken, or retire the claim instead of leaving it permanently trusted.

scenarios.label: Raw auto-block
scenarios.summary: A normalized feed record bypasses enrichment and analyst review, then a permissive policy sends it directly to a preventive control.
scenarios.result: Transport and parsing succeeded, but the decision is unsafe: a source assertion became a high-blast-radius action without enough freshness, context, false-positive, marking, or approval evidence.

scenarios.label: Restricted sharing
scenarios.summary: An analyst validates useful intelligence, but its source marking does not permit release to the configured external consumer.
scenarios.result: The correct outcome is no external release. The platform may support an allowed internal use, but it must not widen the audience merely because TAXII or another connector can reach it.

scenarios.label: Feedback missing
scenarios.summary: A reviewed alert reaches the consumer, but sightings, false positives, and disablement outcomes never return to the knowledge store.
scenarios.result: Distribution still appears healthy, but quality cannot improve and retired intelligence may remain active. Consumer outcomes are part of the intelligence lifecycle, not optional reporting.
